questions.stem: A non-self-supporting ladder reaches a support point 16 feet above the ground. Using the 4-to-1 setup rule, how far should the base be from the support?
options: 2 feet
4 feet
8 feet
12 feet
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The base distance is one foot out for every four feet of vertical height: 16/4 = 4 feet.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This uses an 8-to-1 ratio rather than 4 to 1.
This uses a 2-to-1 ratio and places the base too far out.
This subtracts one quarter of the height instead of dividing by four.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 29, ladder basics and setup, pp. 657-665; OSHA walking-working surfaces

questions.stem: Which practice is acceptable when using a standard stepladder?
options: Lean the folded stepladder against a wall as a straight ladder
Stand on the top cap for additional reach
Fully open and lock the spreaders, then stand only on permitted steps
Move the ladder while a worker remains on it
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Stepladders should be fully opened with spreaders locked and used according to manufacturer step restrictions.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A standard stepladder is designed for use in the open, locked position unless specifically designed otherwise.
The top cap is not a permitted standing step.
Moving an occupied ladder creates a serious fall hazard.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 29, ladders and ladder accident prevention, pp. 658-665; OSHA 1910.23

questions.stem: What is the nominal top-edge height for a general-industry top rail?
options: 30 inches exactly
36 inches, plus or minus 1 inch
48 inches minimum with no tolerance
42 inches, plus or minus 3 inches
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: General-industry top rails are generally 42 inches, plus or minus 3 inches, above the walking-working surface.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Thirty inches is below the required nominal top-edge height.
Thirty-six inches does not meet the general top-rail criterion.
The standard uses a nominal 42-inch height with permitted variation, not a universal 48-inch minimum.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 29, fall protection systems, pp. 675-679; OSHA 1910.29(b)

questions.stem: A new fixed ladder extends 32 feet above a lower level. What protection is required under the modern general-industry ladder provisions?
options: A personal fall-arrest system or ladder safety system
A cage alone is always sufficient for a new ladder
No protection because the ladder is under 40 feet
Only a warning sign at the base
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: New fixed ladders extending more than 24 feet require a personal fall-arrest or ladder safety system.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Cages are being phased out as the sole protection for new fixed ladders subject to the current requirements.
The relevant threshold is more than 24 feet, not 40 feet.
A warning sign does not arrest or prevent a fall.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 29, ladders and fall protection, pp. 657-679; OSHA 1910.28(b)(9)

questions.stem: A temporary floor opening is covered during maintenance. Which condition is most important?
options: The cover is loose so it can be removed quickly
The cover is secured, capable of supporting expected loads, and clearly identified
The cover is made only from a visually contrasting material
The opening is covered only when supervisors are present
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A floor-hole cover must resist expected loading, remain secured against displacement, and be marked or otherwise identified.
incorrectOptionExplanations: An unsecured cover can shift and expose the opening.
Visibility helps but does not establish strength or securement.
Protection must remain effective whenever exposure exists, not only during supervision.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 29, duty to have fall protection and cover criteria, pp. 675-679; OSHA 1910.28 and 1910.29

questions.stem: A fall-arrest setup may involve 6 feet of free fall, 3.5 feet of deceleration, 1.5 feet from the D-ring to the worker feet, and a 2-foot safety margin. What minimum clearance is needed below the anchorage connection level?
options: 9.5 feet
11 feet
13 feet
15 feet
incorrectOptionExplanations: This omits the D-ring-to-feet distance and safety margin.
This omits the safety margin.
This adds an unsupported extra 2 feet to the stated components.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 25 and 29, fall distance and clearance calculations, pp. 583-589 and 676-679
questions.formula: clearance = free fall + deceleration + D-ring-to-feet + safety margin

questions.stem: Before a rope descent system is used for window cleaning, what must be confirmed about the anchorage?
options: It is the nearest roof object regardless of design
It is used only by one worker at a time
It has been painted a designated safety color
It has been identified, tested or certified as capable of supporting the required load
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Rope descent systems require a suitable anchorage with verified capacity, not an improvised attachment point.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Proximity does not establish structural capacity or suitability.
Limiting use to one worker does not establish the required anchorage strength.
Color coding does not verify engineering capacity.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 29, rope descent systems, pp. 670-675; OSHA 1910.27

questions.stem: A distribution area has repeated same-level falls caused by shrink wrap and broken pallets in aisles. Which action is strongest?
options: Redesign material-flow and waste-removal controls so aisles remain continuously clear
Remind employees to watch where they walk
Require slip-resistant shoes as the only control
Wait for the weekly cleanup crew
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A reliable housekeeping system should prevent and promptly remove obstructions as part of the operating process.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Attention reminders do not remove recurring obstructions.
Footwear may reduce some consequences but does not correct aisle hazards.
A weekly schedule permits hazards to remain during normal operations.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 29, general walking-working surface requirements, pp. 657-680
